admission.justification: Absent ignored caches can falsely block a real clone, while silently fixing stale caches or dropping a computed informational count can misrepresent what was checked. Owner-mediated preparation and separate truthful reporting prevent those errors.

applicability: Full memory-quality input preparation, absent/stale route-index cache reporting and informational proof/review projections.
conditions: A full run builds absent derived route-index caches through the existing owner; existing stale cache bytes are left for the actual stale-cache check rather than silently overwritten.
The cache-build result exposes built/error facts independently of quality readiness.
The computed invariantsWithoutProofCount survives report-disabled and mounted sync/completed-poll delivery; proof coverage remains informational, not an actionable finding kind.
Knowledge review is labeled nongating and remains distinct from the actual invariant/worklist gate and complete Curator curation.
exclusions: A built cache or zero proof count is not semantic certification, proof acceptance or a frozen-pair grade.
The original producer's real-clone witness and explicit failed native result remain historical producer evidence; no new run is claimed.
statement: The quality operation builds absent route-index caches through their owner, counts existing stale caches, exposes invariantsWithoutProofCount and labels knowledge review as nongating.
